question: In a certain coded language: A # B means A is the mother of B; A @ B means A is the brother of B; A $ B means A is the wife of B; A % B means A is the father of B. Based on the expression 'P $ Q % R @ S # T', how is P related to T?
explanation: P $ Q means P is the wife of Q. Q % R means Q is the father of R, making P the mother of R. R @ S means R is the brother of S, so S is also the child of P. S # T means S is the mother of T. Since P is the mother of S (who is the mother of T), P is the maternal grandmother of T.
trick: P is female ($) and there are two upward generational shifts (% and #) between P and T, immediately identifying her as a grandmother.
tip: Assign numeric values to generations (+1 for parents) to quickly calculate gaps.

question: Read the following codes carefully: A & B means A is the sister of B; A * B means A is the father of B; A ^ B means A is the mother of B; A ! B means A is the brother of B. Which of the following expressions indicates that 'M is the maternal uncle of N'?
explanation: To be a maternal uncle, M must be male (brother to N's mother). In 'M ! K ^ N', M ! K means M is the brother of K. K ^ N means K is the mother of N. Therefore, M is the brother of N's mother, making him the maternal uncle of N.
trick: Eliminate options where M's gender is female or unknown. '&' makes M female (sister) and '*' makes M a father (wrong generation path).
tip: Check the last symbol attached to the target person to confirm gender first.

question: In a family of 7 members A to G, there are two married couples. The Doctor is the father of C. D is the paternal grandmother of the Student E. F, the Engineer, is the only son of G, who is the father-in-law of the Doctor A. B is the sister of E and daughter of C. How is the Engineer related to C?
explanation: A is the father of C and paternal grandfather to E, making A married to D (paternal grandmother). G is the father-in-law of A, meaning G is the father of A's wife (D). F is the only son of G, so F is D's brother. Since D is C's mother, her brother F (the Engineer) is C's maternal uncle.
trick: G is A's father-in-law, so G is the father of A's wife. F is G's son, making F the brother-in-law of A and uncle to A's child C.
tip: Link professions directly to the letters to avoid tracking two separate variables.

question: Pay attention to the flipped subjects in this code: P + Q means Q is the father of P; P - Q means Q is the mother of P; P / Q means Q is the brother of P; P x Q means Q is the sister of P. In the expression 'J - K / L + M', how is M related to J?
explanation: Read backward due to flipped subjects. J - K means K is the mother of J. K / L means L is the brother of K. L + M means M is the father of L. Since M is the father of L and L is the brother of K, M is the father of K. Since K is J's mother, M is J's maternal grandfather.
trick: Flipped codes mean the right-side entity drives the relationship. Trace from left to right but assign the role to the right-hand letter.
tip: Always circle or highlight if the relationship reads backward (Q is to P).

question: Given the codes: A ? B means A is the father of B; A < B means A is the daughter of B; A > B means A is the brother of B; A = B means A is the wife of B. Which expression establishes that 'X is the sister-in-law of Y'?
explanation: In 'X = Z > Y', X = Z means X is the wife of Z. Z > Y means Z is the brother of Y. Since X is married to Y's brother, X is the sister-in-law of Y.
trick: A sister-in-law must be a female. '=' ensures X is a wife (female). Options where X is '<' (daughter) shift the generation incorrectly.
tip: Look for spouse (=) combined with sibling (>) codes for in-law relations.

question: R is the father of S and T. W is the mother of P. P is married to S. V is the daughter of P. U is the son of T. Q is the husband of V. If P is a woman, how is W related to V?
explanation: P is married to S, and P is a woman, so S is her husband. V is the daughter of P (and S). W is the mother of P. Therefore, W is the mother of V's mother, which makes W the maternal grandmother of V.
trick: The relationship focuses purely on the maternal line: W -> P -> V. The extra information about R, T, U, and Q are distractors.
tip: Isolate the direct path between the two target persons; ignore distractors.

question: Consider these codes (note the mixed directions): A © B means A is the husband of B; A ® B means A is the sister of B; A ™ B means B is the mother of A; A ~ B means B is the brother of A. What symbol must replace the '?' in 'P ® Q ™ R ? S' so that S is the maternal uncle of P?
explanation: P ® Q means P is the sister of Q. Q ™ R means R is the mother of Q (and therefore R is the mother of P). For S to be the maternal uncle of P, S must be the brother of R. The code 'A ~ B' means B is the brother of A. So, 'R ~ S' means S is the brother of R.
trick: Since R is the mother, S must be her brother. The symbol '~' places the brother role on the right-hand entity (S).
tip: Watch carefully which side (left or right) takes the gendered relationship role.

question: A alpha B means A is the father of B; A beta B means A is the mother of B; A gamma B means A is the son of B; A delta B means A is the daughter of B. In the expression 'H alpha I gamma J beta K', how is J related to H?
explanation: H alpha I means H is the father of I. I gamma J means I is the son of J. Since H is the father of I and I is the son of J, H and J must be the parents of I. Since H is male, J must be the mother. Thus, J is the wife of H.
trick: When a child has a defined father (H) and is simultaneously the son of someone else (J), that someone else must be the mother.
tip: Two people pointing to the same child as parents are a married couple.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R are six family members with two married couples. N is the sister of O. R is the brother-in-law of P, who is the mother of N. M is the father of O and grandfather of Q. If Q is a male and O is unmarried, how is Q related to O?
explanation: P is the mother of N and O. M is the father of O, so M and P are married. R is P's brother-in-law (M's brother). M is the grandfather of Q. Since O is unmarried, Q must be the child of N. As Q is male, he is N's son, making him the nephew of O.
trick: Since O is unmarried, the grandchild (Q) must belong to the sibling (N), making Q a nephew or niece. The 'male' constraint confirms Nephew.
tip: Unmarried siblings immediately shift offspring to the other sibling's lineage.

question: A 1 B means A is the father of B; A 2 B means A is the sister of B; A 3 B means A is the wife of B; A 4 B means A is the mother of B. Which expression establishes that 'G is the paternal aunt of H'?
explanation: G must be a female (sister) and in the +1 generation. In 'G 2 X 1 H', G 2 X means G is the sister of X. X 1 H means X is the father of H. Thus, G is the sister of H's father, making her the paternal aunt of H.
trick: Generation math: Aunt is +1. '2' is 0, '1' is +1. Total gap +1. G must be female ('2' ensures she is a sister).
tip: Sum up the numeric generation gaps to filter options instantly.

question: Based on these numeric codes: A 5 B means A is the brother of B; A 6 B means A is the sister of B; A 7 B means A is the father of B; A 8 B means A is the mother of B. In the expression 'K 6 L 7 M 5 N', how is K related to N?
explanation: K 6 L means K is the sister of L. L 7 M means L is the father of M. M 5 N means M is the brother of N (so L is also the father of N). Since K is the sister of L (who is the father of N), K is the paternal aunt of N.
trick: K is female (6) and one generation above M/N (7). Since the link (L) is a father, the aunt relationship is definitively paternal.
tip: Trace the gender of the middle connecting person to determine paternal/maternal.

question: In a family of 6, the ratio of males to females is 1:1. A is the father of B and the grandfather of C. D is the mother of C and the daughter-in-law of F. B is the brother of E, who is unmarried. C is the child of D. How is F related to E?
explanation: A is the grandfather of C and D is the daughter-in-law of F. This means A and F are married, with A being male and F being female. B and E are their children. Since D is the daughter-in-law, she is married to B (as E is unmarried). C is the child of B and D. Since F is the wife of A (the father of E), F is the mother of E.
trick: The 'daughter-in-law' and 'grandfather' dynamic forces A and F to be the top-generation couple. F must be the mother of A's children.
tip: In closed family puzzles, lock in the highest generation pair first.

question: Evaluate these bracket codes: P [ Q means P is the daughter of Q; P ] Q means P is the son of Q; P { Q means P is the wife of Q; P } Q means P is the husband of Q. Based on 'W [ X { Y ] Z', which of the following statements is definitely true?
options: W is the granddaughter of Z
X is the mother-in-law of Z
Y is the uncle of W
Z is the father of W
answer: W is the granddaughter of Z
explanation: W [ X means W is the daughter of X. X { Y means X is the wife of Y (making Y the father of W). Y ] Z means Y is the son of Z. Since Y is the father of W, and Y is the son of Z, W is the granddaughter of Z.
trick: W is in the -2 generation relative to Z (-1 for daughter, 0 for spouse, -1 for son backwards). This makes W a granddaughter.
tip: Map relationships backwards from the target to see the total generational shift.

question: A !! B means A is the father of B; A @@ B means A is the mother of B; A ## B means A is the son of B; A $$ B means A is the daughter of B. Which of the following expressions does NOT indicate that S is a parent of X?
explanation: In 'S @@ X !! T' and 'S @@ X @@ T', S @@ X means S is the mother of X, making S a parent. In 'S @@ X ## T', S @@ X means S is the mother of X, making S a parent as well. Wait, all of them indicate S is a parent! The question asks which does NOT show S is a parent. Since all do, the answer is None of these. (Correction: Let's read carefully, all explicitly start with 'S @@ X', meaning S is the mother of X).
trick: If all options start with 'S @@ X', S is definitively the mother in every single one, so they all show S as a parent.
tip: Don't get distracted by the tail end of the expression if the front proves it.

question: Using complex symbols: A +* B means A is the sister of B; A -* B means A is the brother of B; A /* B means A is the father of B; A =* B means A is the mother of B. In the equation 'L +* M -* N /* O +* P', how is M related to P?
explanation: L +* M means L is the sister of M. M -* N means M is the brother of N. N /* O means N is the father of O. O +* P means O is the sister of P. So, M is the brother of N, who is the father of P. This makes M the paternal uncle of P.
trick: M is male (-*) and is a sibling to N. N is a father (/*) to the lowest generation (O and P). M is the father's brother (paternal uncle).
tip: Ignore prefix entities (like L) if they don't impact the target relation.

question: P || Q means P is the father of Q; P && Q means P is the mother of Q; P == Q means P is the sister of Q; P >> Q means P is the brother of Q. Which expression proves that 'A is the nephew of B'?
explanation: In 'B == C || A >> D', B == C means B is the sister of C. C || A means C is the father of A. A >> D means A is the brother of D. Because A is a male (brother) and his father is B's sibling, A is the nephew of B.
trick: Nephew requires A to be male. In 'B == C || A >> D', the '>>' ensures A is male, and '||' sets him one generation below B's sibling.
tip: Target the gender of the requested individual first to eliminate options.

question: A : B means A is the sibling of B; A ; B means A is the child of B; A , B means A is the spouse of B; A . B means A is the parent of B. In the gender-neutral expression 'M ; N , O . P', how is M related to P?
explanation: M ; N means M is the child of N. N , O means N is the spouse of O. O . P means O is the parent of P. Since N and O are married, and M is the child of N while P is the child of O, M and P share the same parents, making them siblings.
trick: Even though exact genders are hidden, a child of a spouse is a child of the other spouse, confirming a direct sibling relationship.
tip: Translate neutral terms (parent/spouse/child) directly into logical family nodes.

question: In a family of 7 members, there is only one married couple in the first generation. J is the father of K and L. M is the sister-in-law of L and wife of K. N is the son of M. O is the daughter of L. P is the mother-in-law of M. How is P related to O?
explanation: J is the father of K and L. M is the wife of K. Since P is the mother-in-law of M (K's wife), P must be the mother of K (and L). Therefore, J and P are the first-generation couple. O is the daughter of L. Since P is L's mother, P is the grandmother of O.
trick: P is the mother-in-law of a sibling's wife, which translates directly to P being the mother of the siblings. Thus, she is a grandmother to their kids.
tip: Identify the top-generation matriarch/patriarch to quickly solve downward relations.

question: P ^1 Q means P is the father of Q; P ^2 Q means P is the sister of Q; P ^3 Q means P is the brother of Q; P ^4 Q means P is the mother of Q. Which expression proves 'E is the maternal aunt of F'?
explanation: To be a maternal aunt, E must be the sister of F's mother. In 'E ^2 M ^4 F', E ^2 M means E is the sister of M. M ^4 F means M is the mother of F. Therefore, E is the sister of F's mother, making her the maternal aunt.
trick: Maternal aunt is strictly +1 generation female via the mother line. ^2 (sister) provides the female role, ^4 (mother) provides the maternal link.
tip: Read reverse expressions piece by piece backwards to verify.

question: A family consists of 6 people: S, T, U, V, W, X. V is the sister of U. W is the brother of V's husband. X is the father of U and grandfather of T. S is the mother of W. If U is unmarried, how is S related to T?
explanation: V is the sister of U. W is the brother of V's husband. S is the mother of W, which means S is also the mother of V's husband. X is the father of U (and V) and grandfather of T. T is the child of V and her husband. Since S is the mother of V's husband, S is the paternal grandmother of T.
trick: S is the mother of the husband. T is the child of that husband. This cleanly makes S the paternal grandmother regardless of X's lineage.
tip: Focus entirely on the husband's side of the family to resolve S's role.

question: Read the codes: P ♠ Q means P is the brother of Q; P ♣ Q means P is the husband of Q; P ♥ Q means P is the sister of Q; P ♦ Q means P is the son of Q. In the expression 'A ♠ B ♣ C ♥ D ♦ E', how is A related to the husband of C?
explanation: A ♠ B means A is the brother of B. B ♣ C means B is the husband of C. The husband of C is clearly B. Since A is the brother of B, A is simply the brother of C's husband.
trick: The expression continues with C ♥ D ♦ E, but the question only asks for A's relation to C's husband (who is B). The rest is a distractor.
tip: Identify the target individuals first; do not solve the entire chain if unnecessary.

question: Directional codes: A UP B means A is the brother of B; A DOWN B means A is the sister of B; A LEFT B means A is the father of B; A RIGHT B means A is the mother of B. Which expression establishes that 'M is the paternal aunt of N'?
explanation: To be a paternal aunt, M must be the sister of N's father. Let the father be F. M DOWN F means M is the sister of F. F LEFT N means F is the father of N. Combining them gives M DOWN F LEFT N.
trick: M must be female, so she must be followed by DOWN or RIGHT. An aunt is +1 generation, requiring one horizontal move (DOWN) and one vertical move (LEFT) towards N.
tip: Map 'paternal aunt' to 'father's sister' and translate sequentially backward.

question: In a family of 7 members (A, B, C, D, E, F, G), B is the mother of F and the mother-in-law of E. D is the sister of C and the daughter of E. A is the father of C. G is the unmarried brother-in-law of A. How is G related to D?
explanation: Since A is the father of C, and E is the mother of C and D, A and E are married. B is the mother-in-law of E, making B the mother of A. G is the unmarried brother-in-law of A, meaning G is the brother of A's wife, E. Since G is E's brother and E is D's mother, G is D's maternal uncle.
trick: G is the brother of D's mother. In Indian puzzles, 'unmarried brother-in-law of husband' immediately points to the wife's brother.
tip: Link spouses together first (A and E) to anchor the rest of the family tree.

question: Watch the flipped subjects: P ₹ Q means P is the husband of Q; P £ Q means P is the daughter of Q; P € Q means P is the sister of Q; P ¥ Q means Q is the mother of P. Based on 'A ₹ B £ C ¥ D € E', how is D related to A?
explanation: A ₹ B means A is the husband of B. B £ C means B is the daughter of C. C ¥ D means D is the mother of C (flipped relation). Since D is the mother of C, and C is the parent of B, D is the grandmother of B. Since A is B's husband, D is A's grandmother-in-law.
trick: The ¥ symbol flips the flow from left-to-right to right-to-left. D becomes the active mother figure for C.
tip: Draw arrows indicating the direction of the relationship for each symbol to avoid flipping.

question: A STAR B means A is the father of B; A HASH B means A is the mother of B; A DASH B means A is the brother of B; A SLASH B means A is the sister of B. What symbol should replace the '?' in 'M STAR N DASH O ? P HASH Q' to ensure M is the maternal grandfather of Q?
explanation: P HASH Q means P is the mother of Q. For M to be Q's maternal grandfather, M must be P's father. M STAR N makes M the father of N. N DASH O makes N the brother of O, meaning M is also O's father. If O DASH P (brother) or O SLASH P (sister), P becomes a sibling of O and N, making M the father of P.
trick: The symbol only needs to establish a horizontal sibling link between O and P. Both DASH (brother) and SLASH (sister) work perfectly without altering P's gender.
tip: Sibling operators act as bridges that do not change the generational height.

question: Given the codes: P a Q means P is the wife of Q; P b Q means P is the brother of Q; P c Q means P is the daughter of Q; P d Q means P is the son of Q. In the expression 'J c K a L b M d N a O', which of the following statements is definitely FALSE?
options: L is the uncle of J
K is the sister-in-law of M
N is the paternal grandfather of J
M is the uncle of J
answer: N is the paternal grandfather of J
explanation: J c K means J is daughter of K. K a L means K is wife of L (L is J's father). L b M means L is brother of M. M d N means M is son of N. N a O means N is wife of O. Thus, N is female (grandmother). Stating N is a grandfather is definitely false.
trick: The final connection 'N a O' definitively makes N a female (wife). Thus any statement calling N a grandfather is a direct contradiction.
tip: Check the very last symbol attached to a person to confirm their gender.

question: In a family of 8, there are 3 married couples. The eldest member, H, is a widow and has only one daughter, N, who is a spinster. H also has a son, M, married to P. P has a son Q and a daughter R. Q is married to S. How is H related to S?
explanation: H is the widow and mother of M (son) and N (daughter). M is married to P, so M and P are parents of Q and R. Q is married to S, making S the wife of Q. Since H is the mother of M, who is the father of Q, H is Q's grandmother. Since S is Q's wife, H is S's grandmother-in-law.
trick: The terms 'spinster' and 'widow' are pure gender and marital status clues. H is the top-tier female, mapping directly down to the third-tier spouse.
tip: Trace the direct lineage path first, then add the in-law suffix for spouses.

question: A (X) B means A is the mother of B; A (Y) B means A is the sister of B; A (Z) B means A is the father of B; A (W) B means A is the brother of B. Which expression shows that 'C is the paternal aunt of D'?
explanation: To be a paternal aunt, C must be the sister of D's father. In 'C (Y) E (Z) D', C (Y) E means C is the sister of E. E (Z) D means E is the father of D. Therefore, C is the sister of D's father, which perfectly defines a paternal aunt.
trick: C must be a sister (Y) to a male who is a father (Z). Only the combination (Y) followed by (Z) creates the specific paternal aunt generation shift.
tip: Match the specific relation (Aunt) to its atomic parts (Sister of Father).

question: Arrow logic codes: A <-> B means A is the wife of B; A -> B means A is the father of B; A <- B means A is the mother of B; A -- B means A is the sister of B. In 'W <-> X -> Y <- Z', how is W related to Z?
explanation: W <-> X means W is the wife of X. X -> Y means X is the father of Y, making W the mother of Y. Y <- Z means Y is the mother of Z. Since W is the mother of Y, and Y is the mother of Z, W is the maternal grandmother of Z.
trick: The combination of X -> Y (X is father) and Y <- Z (Y is mother) can be confusing. It just means Y is a mother to Z, but a child to X.
tip: Read arrow directions strictly as 'Subject operator Object' to avoid logic tangles.

question: A man points to a photo and says, 'The person in this photo is W, defined by the equation X AND Y OR Z NOT W'. If P AND Q means P is the father of Q; P OR Q means P is the only son of Q; P NOT Q means P is the mother of Q. If W is the man's wife, how is X related to the man?
explanation: X AND Y means X is the father of Y. Y OR Z means Y is the only son of Z. This makes X and Z married, with X as the father and Z as the mother of Y. Z NOT W means Z is the mother of W. So, Y and W are siblings. Since Y is the 'only son', W must be a daughter. X is W's father. Since W is the man's wife, X is the man's father-in-law.
trick: The phrase 'only son' means any other child (like W) must be female. W is a daughter, leading directly to the in-law relationship.
tip: Pay close attention to restrictive words like 'only son' to deduce genders of siblings.

question: A family has 6 members: P, Q, R, S, T, U. There are two married couples. T is the mother of the only daughter of S. Q is the paternal grandfather of U. R is the brother-in-law of S, who has no siblings. P is female. If U is male, how is P related to R?
explanation: S has no siblings, so his brother-in-law R must be his wife's brother. T is the mother of S's daughter, so T is S's wife, and R is T's brother. Q is U's paternal grandfather, meaning Q is S's father (since U is male, likely S's son). Since P is female and there are two couples, P is Q's wife and S's mother. R is the brother of S's wife. Therefore, P is the mother of R's brother-in-law (S).
trick: You must define the two couples first (Q&P, S&T). Then map the cross-family relation purely descriptively.
tip: When standard terms fail, trace the literal descriptive path (Mother of Husband).

question: Using angled bracket codes: A <+> B means A is the son of B; A <-> B means A is the daughter of B; A <*> B means A is the brother of B; A </> B means A is the sister of B. Which expression denotes 'G is the nephew of H'?
explanation: A nephew is the son of a sibling. G must be a son (<+>) of someone (X). That someone (X) must be a sibling (like a brother, <*>) to H. G <+> X means G is the son of X. X <*> H means X is the brother of H. Thus, G is the son of H's brother, making him a nephew.
trick: G must directly connect to a child-operator (<+>) to establish the downward generational shift required for a nephew.
tip: Find the code that gives the target the correct gender and generation gap immediately.

question: Generational markers: P T1 Q means P is 1 generation above Q and male; P T2 Q means P is 1 generation above Q and female; P T3 Q means P is same generation as Q and male; P T4 Q means P is same generation as Q and female. In 'X T2 Y T3 Z T1 W', how is X related to W?
explanation: X T2 Y means X is the mother/aunt of Y. Y T3 Z means Y is the brother/cousin of Z. Z T1 W means Z is the father/uncle of W. Assuming direct standard relations (as is common unless specified): X is mother of Y, Y is brother of Z, making X the mother of Z. Since Z is the father of W, X is the paternal grandmother of W.
trick: Sum the generations: X is +1 to Y. Y is 0 to Z. Z is +1 to W. Total is +2. X is female (T2). Female +2 generation = Grandmother. The intermediate link Z is male (T1), so it's Paternal.
tip: Add generation values to instantly calculate the total family tree height.

question: A ++ B means A is the sister of B; A -- B means A is the mother of B; A ** B means A is the brother of B; A // B means A is the father of B. Based on the equation 'A -- B ** C // D ++ E', how is A related to E?
explanation: A -- B means A is the mother of B. B ** C means B is the brother of C. C // D means C is the father of D. D ++ E means D is the sister of E. Since C is the father of D and E, and A is the mother of C (via B), A is the mother of their father. Thus, A is the paternal grandmother of E.
trick: D and E are at the lowest generation. C is their father. A is the mother of C. The intermediate sibling B doesn't alter the vertical lineage.
tip: Skip over horizontal sibling links (**, ++) when tracking direct vertical ancestry.

question: Family of 7: A is the mother of B and C. D is the son-in-law of A. E is the only grandson of A. F is the unmarried sister-in-law of D. G is the wife of E. If the family has exactly two daughters in the second generation, how is B related to E?
explanation: A has children B and C. D is the son-in-law, meaning he is married to one of A's daughters. F is the unmarried sister-in-law of D, so F must be the sister of D's wife. Thus, A's children are the married daughter and F. Therefore, B and C must represent the wife and F. If B is the wife of D, then B is the mother of D's son E. (If C was the wife, it would be symmetric, but 'Mother' is the only valid option for the relationship).
trick: The unmarried sister-in-law (F) must be the other sibling. This forces B to be the married daughter who produced the grandson E.
tip: In-law constraints with 'unmarried' siblings usually force a strict married-couple deduction.

question: Greek logic: P α Q means P is the husband of Q; P β Q means P is the sister of Q; P γ Q means P is the mother of Q; P δ Q means P is the brother of Q. Which expression proves 'X is the maternal aunt of Y'?
explanation: A maternal aunt is the sister of one's mother. In 'X β M γ Y', X β M means X is the sister of M. M γ Y means M is the mother of Y. Therefore, X is the sister of Y's mother, validating her as the maternal aunt.
trick: X must be female (β) and horizontally linked to the vertical mother connection (γ). Any other arrangement breaks the generation or gender rule.
tip: Build the exact required chain backward in your head before checking options.

question: Consider these punctuation codes: A :: B means A is the daughter of B; A ;; B means A is the son of B; A ,, B means A is the wife of B; A .. B means B is the husband of A. Based on 'K :: L ,, M ;; N', how is N related to K?
explanation: K :: L means K is the daughter of L. L ,, M means L is the wife of M, meaning M is the father of K. M ;; N means M is the son of N. Since N is the parent of M (who is K's father), N is the paternal grandparent of K.
trick: N's gender is completely unknown. However, since N is the parent of M (the father), the 'Paternal Grandparent' designation is accurate regardless of gender.
tip: Do not assume gender at the end of a chain; use neutral terms like Grandparent.

question: Double-step codes: P [+] Q means P is the grandfather of Q; P [-] Q means P is the grandmother of Q; P [*] Q means P is the grandson of Q; P [/] Q means P is the granddaughter of Q. If 'A [+] B [*] C' is true, which of the following MUST be true?
options: A is the husband of C
A and C belong to the same generation
C is the grandmother of B
